name: Lethal Multiple Congenital Anomalies/Dysmorphic Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Lethal Multiple Congenital Anomalies/Dysmorphic Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of multiple major congenital malformations affecting at least two organ systems
Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphic features including micrognathia, hypertelorism, and low-set ears
Prenatal lethality or death within the neonatal period due to multisystem involvement
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with developmental pathways (if available)
Exclusion of other syndromes with overlapping features by clinical and genetic evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple major congenital malformations with characteristic dysmorphic features and prenatal lethality or neonatal death
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing may support but is not always available.

searchTerms: severe facial abnormalities including small jaw
marked facial malformations with small chin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple major congenital malformations involving cardiovascular and renal systems
searchTerms: multiple major birth defects affecting heart and kidneys
congenital malformations involving cardiovascular and renal systems

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prenatal or neonatal lethality due to multisystem organ failure
searchTerms: death before or shortly after birth from organ failure
prenatal or neonatal death due to multisystem failure
early lethality from multiple organ problems
ears set low and abnormally shaped
unusually shaped ears placed low on head

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects including ventricular septal defects

laboratory: Abnormal metabolic screening in some cases
Elevated markers of organ dysfunction in neonatal period
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing multiple structural anomalies
Postnatal echocardiography revealing congenital heart defects
Renal ultrasound demonstrating hypoplasia or agenesis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in developmental genes (variable and not fully characterized)
Negative results for common syndromic causes in some cases
other: Prenatal diagnosis often possible via detailed anomaly scan
Neonatal death typically occurs within first days of life

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic clenched hands with overlapping fingers

redFlags: Multiple major congenital malformations detected prenatally
Neonatal respiratory failure due to pulmonary hypoplasia
